statements.t: I believe combining MaxCyte and Akron will expand our commercial opportunity, strengthen our financial profile, and drive long-term value,” said Maher Masoud, President and CEO of MaxCyte.

“MaxCyte’s third quarter results reflect the progress that we have made throughout 2026, with approximately 15% year-over-year core revenue growth expected in the second half of this year, exceeding the growth expectations we established at the beginning of 2026.

Because it excludes the cash purchase price, deal-related expenses and other costs related to the Akron acquisition, it is not a forecast of the Company’s actual year-end cash position, and the Company does not expect to hold approximately $133 million of total cash, cash equivalents and investments as of December 31, 2026.

Supported by expert scientific, technical and regulatory guidance, our platform empowers researchers to engineer diverse cell types and payloads, accelerating the development of safe and effective treatments for human health.

dropped.t: “Preliminary third quarter and total second half revenue is ahead of our expectations, and we updated our core business revenue guidance to reflect approximately 15% year-over-year growth in the second half of 2026,” said Maher Masoud, President and CEO of MaxCyte.

We entered into 2026 with the goal of getting back to growth in the second half and we are very encouraged by our return to double-digit growth, with meaningful outperformance in the third quarter driven by accelerated instrument purchasing from a large customer, which we originally anticipated to occur in the fourth quarter.
In addition, we raised our SPL Program-related revenue guidance after recognizing a milestone from one of our SPL partners, our second milestone achieved in 2026.

statements.t: • our expected future growth and the success of our business model;
• the expected future growth of our manufacturing capabilities and sales, support and marketing capabilities;
Our assay services provide gene editing risk assessment services using highly sensitive assays to detect on-target and off-target gene editing effects (“Assay Services”).

We expect to continue to incur net losses as we focus on growing commercial sales of our cell enabling solutions in both the U.S. and international markets, including expanding our sales force, scaling our manufacturing operations, and continuing research and development efforts to develop new products and further enhance our existing products.

By combining Akron Bio's established portfolio of GMP-grade reagents and ancillary materials with our cell-engineering platform, we expect to significantly expand our addressable market, strengthen our financial profile, and accelerate our path to profitability.

If completed, we expect the acquisition to increase our revenue, operating expenses, amortization of acquired intangibles and interest expense, to result in goodwill and intangible assets, and to result in additional acquisition-related and integration costs.
We have incurred, and will continue to incur, acquisition-related costs whether or not the acquisition closes.
operating cash flows, which we anticipate will contribute to our combined liquidity and support our progress toward profitability.
We expect to initially draw down $20.0 million from tranche one of the Term Loan and $2.0 million from the Revolver, in each case at the closing of the acquisition.

The credit facility is subject to the execution of definitive loan documentation and other conditions, including the closing of the acquisition, and is expected to contain affirmative and negative covenants, which may limit our operating flexibility.

SPL milestone and royalty revenue continue to experience variability, although we anticipate that variability may moderate as the volume of SPL partnerships and associated milestones grows and matures.

We expect total revenue to increase over time as our customers’ programs advance through the cell therapy lifecycle and our markets grow, resulting in additional instrument revenue, PA revenue and license revenue, and also as the percentage of our installed base that are under SPL license agreements increases.

We expect, however, that our revenue may fluctuate from period-to-period due to the timing of securing product sales and licenses, the inherently uncertain nature of the timing of our partners’ achievements of clinical progress, and our dependence on the program decisions of our partners.
We expect that our cost of goods sold will generally increase or decrease modestly as our instrument, PA and Assay Service revenue increases or decreases.

We expect our gross margin to benefit from realization of milestone and royalty revenue from our SPL agreements, to the extent that such revenue grows to be a significant proportion of overall revenues, as there is no cost of goods sold associated with such revenue.

We expect to continue to incur substantial research and development expenses as we invest in research and development to support our customers, develop new uses for our existing technology and develop improved and/or new offerings to our customers and partners.
We expect these expenses to vary from period to period as a percentage of revenue.

We expect our recurring sales and marketing expenses to increase in absolute dollars in future periods as we expand our commercial sales, marketing and business development teams, expand our product offerings, expand our collaboration efforts, increase our presence globally, and increase marketing activities to drive awareness and adoption of our products.
We expect that in the near term, sales and marketing expenses could increase as a percentage of revenue, and thereafter vary from period to period as a percentage of revenue.
We expect that our general and administrative expenses will increase in absolute dollars in future periods, primarily to support anticipated growth in the business.

We expect to incur operating losses in the near term as we continue to invest in expanding our business through increased sales and marketing efforts, continued research and development, product development, and expansion of our product offerings.
We have based this estimate on assumptions that may prove to be wrong, and we could utilize our available capital resources sooner than we expect.
We expect to fund the $105.0 million closing cash consideration for our proposed acquisition of Akron Bio using existing cash, cash equivalents and investments.
We expect to initially draw down $22.0 million when the debt financing agreement is executed and the acquisition closes.

The proposed acquisition is expected to significantly reduce our cash and investment balances and impact our future cash requirements, including integration costs, debt service obligations and deferred consideration payments.
However, Akron Bio is expected to generate positive operating cash flows, which we anticipate will contribute to our combined liquidity and support our progress toward profitability.
We expect to be able to fund our obligations under these leases, both in the short-term and in the long-term, from cash on hand, investments and operating cash flows.

We have the obligation, if certain revenue targets are achieved, to pay an amount not to exceed $2.5 million to former holders of convertible promissory notes of SeQure for the year ended December 31, 2025 and year ending December 31, 2026.

The cash-flow projections used in the recoverability assessment require management judgment in developing assumptions regarding future revenues, operating costs, customer retention and purchasing activity, and expected disposition value.

The recoverability determination is sensitive to assumptions related to our customers’ ability to achieve specified contractual development milestones and commercial sales-based royalties, as the timing and achievement of those revenues directly affect projected future cash flows.
During the first quarter of the nine months ended September 30, 2026, certain changes in customer milestone forecast assumptions resulted in an evaluation of recoverability of our long-lived assets.

Future impairment conclusions could change if actual results differ from our assumptions or if adverse developments occur with respect to the customer’s progress toward achieving contractual milestones, customer demand, or expected disposition values.

We have outstanding performance stock unit awards ("PSUs") granted in 2024 and 2025 that are subject to the achievement of specified performance targets through December 31, 2026 and December 31, 2027, respectively.
Our proposed acquisition, if completed, could impact our assessment of the probability of achieving these performance targets.

We also intend to rely on other exemptions provided by the JOBS Act, including not being required to comply with the auditor attestation requirements of Section 404(b) of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002.

We will remain an EGC until the earliest of: (i) December 31, 2026, which is the last day of the fiscal year following the fifth anniversary of our IPO in the U.S.; (ii) the last day of the first fiscal year in which our annual gross revenue is $1.235 billion or more; (iii) the date on which we have, during the previous rolling three-year period, issued more than $1 billion in non-convertible debt securities; and…
The Company expects to cease qualifying as an EGC on December 31, 2026, the last day of the fiscal year which is the fifth anniversary of the first sale of its registered common equity.

We expect to remain a smaller reporting company at the time we cease to be an emerging growth company, and expect to continue to rely on exemptions from certain disclosure requirements that are available to smaller reporting companies.
